summary: Kempsey Airport (KPS/YKMP) is a regional airport serving the town of Kempsey on the Mid North Coast of New South Wales, Australia. Located in the Macleay Valley, it primarily supports general aviation, recreational flying, and occasional emergency services operations. The facility provides an important link for the local community in this coastal region approximately 450 kilometres north of Sydney.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Kempsey Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves general aviation activities including private flying, flight training, and emergency services such as the Rural Fire Service and Westpac Life Saver Rescue Helicopter.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights at Kempsey Airport?
A: Scheduled commercial passenger services are very limited; travellers typically use Port Macquarie Airport for regular commercial flights.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a sealed runway, basic pilot facilities, refuelling capabilities, and aircraft parking areas, but limited passenger amenities.

Q: Can private aircraft land at Kempsey Airport?
A: Yes, the airport welcomes private and general aviation aircraft, with pilots required to coordinate arrivals through standard radio or notification procedures.
transport_tips: The airport is located a short drive from Kempsey town centre, approximately 5 kilometres to the south. Renting a car from Port Macquarie or arranging a taxi in advance are the most practical options, as there is no regular public bus service to the terminal. Visitors driving can reach the airport via the Pacific Highway and local road connections.
local_tip: If visiting the area, combine your trip with a drive along the scenic Macleay Valley coastline, including Crescent Head and South West Rocks, which are within easy reach of the airport and showcase some of the best beaches on the NSW Mid North Coast.
